title: Researcher, Robot Motion Planning
organization: School of Engineering, SFBU · Advisor: Dr. Satarupa Mukherjee
description: Ran 30,000+ simulated trials characterizing failure modes of goal-biased RRT (Rapidly-exploring Random Tree) motion planning across parameterized maze environments, varying one parameter at a time to isolate causal effects.

Found that a single obstacle blocking the direct start-to-goal path cuts planner success by 68% (77.8% → 24.7%), and that the best step size depends on the environment rather than being a global constant.
Validated results with multiple independent statistical tests and a held-out 1,000-trial replication; first-author paper in preparation.

title: Founding Member, DevOps AI Engineer
description: Cut assistant response time 58% (60s → 25s) by splitting each query across a multi-agent pipeline (Pydantic AI) that routes every subtask to a specialized agent.

Architected the company's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so AI features request structured context from internal tools and data stores, with role-based access control and explicit handling when retrieval returns nothing.
Owned integration work between MCP surfaces and product APIs: tool schemas, auth boundaries, and failure modes.
Provisioned GCP infrastructure—Compute Engine for workloads that need persistent VMs, Cloud Run for HTTP services, Cloud SQL for relational state—tuning hosting cost and cold-start latency.
Iterated on chunking, indexing, and evaluation loops as new assistant capabilities shipped.

title: IT Student Staff
organization: San Francisco Bay University — IT Department

title: LLM Research and Implementation Intern
description: Built a LangChain + FAISS RAG pipeline that answers staff questions over internal documents with citations, cutting repeat questions between coworkers by 20%.

Benchmarked 5 open-source LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen, Deepseek) against proprietary APIs on latency, token cost, and answer quality, using the same automated evaluation for each before recommending one for deployment.
Refined prompt templates and retrieval settings (top-k, filters, stop sequences) to reduce hallucinations, checking every change against a fixed regression set.
Documented pipeline configuration and failure cases so full-time engineers could extend or debug the stack after the internship.
